conflict_topics: strong-smelling cooking (devil curry) in shared flat
smell infiltrating bedrooms and laundry in service yard
interference with work calls in living room
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants discuss concrete constraints (work calls, laundry drying) and propose specific scheduling solutions rather than only asserting positions.
Agent D demonstrates iterative concessions (notice, time shift, reduced frequency) in response to others' reasons.
C introduces an important technical constraint (wet laundry won't dry indoors) that changes feasible solutions.
Conversation remains focused on practical accommodations with little off-topic repetition.
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of the run the parties had negotiated a concrete compromise proposal but not all parties had explicitly accepted it. Agent D offered several concessions: to give prior notice ("I'll still give you a heads-up" — Turn 12), to cook after 7 p.m. ("I'll cook after 7 p.m., and I'll still give you a heads-up" — Turn 12) — which Agent A accepted ("Okay, that works for me." — Turn 13) — and to reduce frequency to once a week (Turn 17). Agent B agreed to be notified and offered a personal mitigation ("Just let me know before you start, and I can do that." — Turn 19). Agent C provided her laundry schedule ("I do my laundry on Monday, Wednesday and Friday evenings." — Turn 28), and Agent D then proposed moving cooking to Saturday evenings ("So, what if I only cook it on Saturday evenings? Would that work for everyone?" — Turn 29). These moves represent a compromise by Agent D (time, frequency, and notice) and partial accommodations by others, but the transcript ends before all roommates explicitly accept the Saturday-evening plan, so the settlement is not fully confirmed.
position_change_notes: Agent A: retained core demand (no disruptive smell during calls) but accepted time-based accommodation (agreed to after-7pm, Turn 13).

Agent D: shifted from defending regular cooking to proposing multiple accommodations — prior notice (Turn 10/12), after-7pm cooking (Turn 12), reduced frequency (Turn 17), and Saturday-only proposal (Turn 29).
Agent B: initially aligned with A/C's complaint, then proposed a personal mitigation (shut door/open window) and agreed to be notified (Turn 19).
Agent C: maintained concern about laundry-drying and provided concrete schedule information (Turn 28); did not accept Saturday proposal in the transcript.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A requested that nobody cook strong-smelling food (opening); Agents B and C immediately agreed that the smell affects their rooms and laundry (Turns 2-3).

Agent D defended cooking as 'my home food' and apologized that it bothered others (Turn 4), while Agent A said the smell is a real problem for work calls in the living room (Turn 5) — opposing claims about whether the cooking should occur.

Agent D asked for details about A's calls (Turn 6) and A said calls are on weekdays until about 7 p.m. (Turn 7) — the parties moved toward identifying a possible accommodation, but the substantive incompatibility remained.
Agents B and C stated that shifting cooking time doesn't solve the problem because the smell still gets into their rooms and the laundry (Turns 8-9), broadening the set of conflicting interests.

Agent D proposed warning before cooking so others could take in laundry (Turn 10); Agent A said that helps the laundry but does not solve the living-room smell during calls (Turn 11) — a concrete partial proposal, but still insufficient for A.
Agent D offered to cook after 7 p.m. with a heads-up (Turn 12) and Agent A accepted that arrangement (Turn 13), resolving A's immediate schedule conflict but leaving other concerns outstanding.
When D asked B and C (Turn 14), Agent B replied the after-7pm proposal does not solve the issue for her room because the smell still gets in (Turn 16), reopening the unresolved practical conflicts.

Agent D offered to limit the cooking to once a week (Turn 17); Agent B said once a week is better and offered a personal mitigation (shut door and open window) if given prior notice (Turn 19). This reduced intensity but did not settle laundry/drying concerns.

Agent D agreed to B's plan and sought C's view (Turn 20); Agent C raised a new practical objection that bringing wet laundry into her room would prevent drying and create dampness (Turn 21), creating a fresh incompatibility.
Agent B endorsed C's concern (Turn 23) and Agent D acknowledged and asked about a better timing/day for laundry (Turn 25), showing willingness to adjust but with no settled arrangement yet.

Agent A reported being out all day Saturday (Turn 26); Agent B observed that this helps the living-room issue but laundry could still be out on Saturday (Turn 27). The exchange provided information but left issues unresolved.

Agent C gave her laundry schedule (Mon/Wed/Fri evenings, Turn 28) and Agent D proposed to cook only on Saturday evenings (Turn 29). The proposal, if accepted, would avoid most conflicts raised so far, but explicit acceptance by all parties is not yet recorded.

substantive_insights: A's primary problem is timing: client calls until ~7 p.m.; shifting cooking later addresses that concern.
Laundry-drying times are a separate constraint that make a simple 'bring laundry in during cooking' solution infeasible for C.
B is willing to mitigate personal exposure by closing her door and opening a window if given prior notice.
D is willing to change practice substantially (time, frequency, prior notice) to accommodate others, enabling a feasible compromise (Saturday evenings).
